split: stratified 60/20/20; train_test_split random_state=seed then seed+1; sorted indices
primary_metric: unweighted macro-average precision across conditions missing_rate=[0,.1,.3,.5] per seed; then mean across three seeds
control: median imputation fitted on clean training rows + HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=120,max_leaf_nodes=31,learning_rate=.1,random_state=seed), trained on clean train rows
mechanism_ablation: same HGB and train-only median; compare candidate (all training rows masked at rate .20, plus 20 mask features) to augmentation_value_only (same masked rows, no mask columns). Secondary ablation uses mask columns but no training-time masking.
corruption: MCAR; identical evaluation mask draws across methods per seed/rate; RNG=seed+100000+int(rate*1000). Training mask RNG=seed+8000.
pass_fail_rule: Supported pilot only if candidate macro AP exceeds both clean median-impute control and value-only mask augmentation by >=0.01, candidate beats value-only augmentation on >=2/3 seed-level macro means, and mean clean AP is no more than .01 below value-only augmentation. Otherwise no_gain. No held-out tuning.
deviation: A first implementation mistakenly duplicated clean and masked training rows and was used to inspect held-out scores. It was archived as results-superseded-unfaithful.json, corrected based on a faithful reading of the proposal (mask all training rows), and not used to choose hyperparameters. Corrected held-out result is exploratory due this prior test exposure.
limitations: Synthetic MCAR evaluation does not instantiate informative/MNAR assumption; this cannot establish utility under informative missingness.
